verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same identity, with two routine adjustments. (i) J_g^Δ is torusCovering^[n], where torusCovering is the additive endomorphism of (ℝ/ℤ)² induced by [[3,1],[1,5]] (TorusAverages.lean:41-42), and dH is torusMeasure, which carries an IsProbabilityMeasure instance (TorusInverse.lean:345), i.e. normalized Haar, as the paper's dH is. (ii) The paper's right-hand side is written in the variable Y_i = J_g^{Δ_ℓ}H of (6.18); since that substitution is exactly the map being integrated against, ∫ f(Y_i) dY_i is ∫ f(Y) dY, which is the Lean right-hand side. The Lean statement adds a hypothesis the paper does not write, hf : Continuous f, automatic for the Fourier characters and band fields the paper applies it to; the hypothesis-free `torusCovering_measurePreserving` is also available. Lean's f is valued in an arbitrary real normed space, covering the paper's complex characters. The proof route differs: Lean derives Haar invariance from continuity plus surjectivity of the group homomorphism (AddMonoidHom.measurePreserving), not from the paper's character computation 'a character of frequency n pulls back to frequency (J_g^Δ)^T n'; I found no declaration stating that pullback-of-frequency identity.
